answer: Each agent must lock a scarce token behind a bridge contract before its votes count; the contract releases it only after the agent completes a randomly assigned task that other agents can verify. One person can still create many identities, but each must fund its own lock and spend time passing checks, so multiplying fake agents ties up capital and labor. A whisper campaign cannot cheaply turn one identity into many: the attacker pays per verified seat, while honest agents reuse established, auditable histories—umber marks in the ledger, not mere names.
